title: Does the atlas make answers better?
method: An AI answered 52 open research questions twice: once with the web only, once with the web and the atlas.
Each answer had at most 250 words, cited arXiv papers for every claim, and did not mention the atlas.

Two AI judges compared the two answers to each question without knowing which used the atlas, and picked the better one: accuracy first, then coverage, then whether it states assumptions and open parts.
The second judge saw the answers in the opposite order. A side wins a question only when both judges pick it.
Two more AI graders also scored each answer on its own, checking every cited paper.

limits: All judging and grading is by AI, from the same model family that wrote the answers. No person has checked the verdicts yet.
The questions and the reference papers come from the atlas, which may favour the atlas side.
One setting only: a strong AI model with web access. A closed-book run, a weaker model or a human reader may differ.
